name: USB-C USB 2.0 Device Port (power + data, ESD, fuse)
description: 16-pin USB-C receptacle wired as a USB 2.0 sink: 5.1 kΩ CC pull-downs, USBLC6-2SC6 ESD on D+/D− and VBUS, 500 mA polyfuse and VBUS bulk capacitor. Feeds native-USB MCUs (ESP32-S3/C3/C6) or a USB-UART bridge.

components.notes: Common JLCPCB-assembled 16-pin mid-profile receptacle; any 16P USB 2.0 receptacle with the same pad names fits
CC1 pull-down (Rd) — 5.1 kΩ ±1% identifies the port as a sink; one per CC pin, never shared
Low-capacitance ESD array; route D+/D− through pins 1–6 and 3–4 (flow-through)
Resettable fuse, 500 mA hold, ≥6 V rating — size hold current to your load
VBUS bulk, X5R ≥10 V. USB limits total VBUS capacitance at attach to 10 µF

design_notes: Both D+ pins (A6, B6) and both D− pins (A7, B7) must be joined — that is what makes the plug reversible. Never tie CC1 and CC2 to one resistor. Shield is tied straight to GND here; for EMC-sensitive products use 1 MΩ ∥ 4.7 nF to GND instead. SBU1/SBU2 are unused for USB 2.0.
layout_notes: Route D+/D− as a 90 Ω differential pair (use calc_impedance), keep them length-matched within 0.15 mm and away from the board edge. Place the ESD array within 5 mm of the connector, between the connector and everything else. Give VBUS/GND short, wide traces.

name: 3.3 V 600 mA LDO (AP2112K-3.3)
description: AP2112K-3.3 LDO in SOT-23-5 with enable tied to input, ceramic input/output capacitors. Good for ESP32 modules from USB 5 V or a single Li-ion cell at moderate load.

components.notes: 600 mA, ~250 mV typical dropout at 600 mA
Output, X5R ≥6.3 V (datasheet minimum 1 µF); 10 µF holds the rail through Wi-Fi TX bursts

design_notes: Check dissipation with calc_regulator_thermal: from 5 V at 500 mA the LDO burns 0.85 W, far beyond what SOT-23-5 can shed — use a buck converter above ~250 mA from 5 V. From a Li-ion cell, the output drops out of regulation once the cell falls below ~3.55 V at full load.
layout_notes: Put C_IN and C_OUT within 2 mm of their pins with a direct ground return; widen VIN/VOUT traces per calc_trace_width; add copper on the GND pin for heat.
references: Diodes Inc. AP2112 datasheet, Typical Application

name: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 Core (EN reset, BOOT, native USB)
description: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 module with Espressif's recommended EN RC delay (10 kΩ / 1 µF), RESET and BOOT buttons, GPIO0 pull-up, supply decoupling, and reserved 22 Ω series resistors on the native USB lines (GPIO19 = D−, GPIO20 = D+). Pair with usb_c_usb2_device and a 3.3 V regulator.

components.notes: Pick the flash/PSRAM variant you need; R8 (octal PSRAM) variants reserve GPIO35–37
Bulk at the module 3V3 pin for Wi-Fi TX current peaks (X5R ≥6.3 V)
EN delay capacitor — never leave EN floating
Hold while pressing RESET to enter download mode
Reserved USB D− series resistor, place close to the module
Reserved USB D+ series resistor, place close to the module

design_notes: Strapping pins: GPIO0 (pulled up here), GPIO3, GPIO45 and GPIO46. Keep GPIO45 low at reset: unless the VDD_SPI eFuse has been burned, GPIO45 = 1 selects 1.8 V VDD_SPI and a module with 3.3 V flash will not boot. Keep GPIO46 low at reset. Do not hang large capacitance on GPIO0. With octal-PSRAM (R8) modules GPIO35, GPIO36 and GPIO37 are not available. GPIO19/GPIO20 are taken by native USB when it is used. Add a 499 Ω series resistor on U0TXD if it leaves the board. Supply needs ≥500 mA headroom.
layout_notes: Put the antenna at or past the board edge with no copper, traces or components under it on any layer — follow the module datasheet's keep-out drawing exactly. Place C_BULK/C_DEC at pin 2, the EN RC close to pin 3, and stitch the module ground pad to the ground plane with many vias.
references: Espressif ESP32-S3 Hardware Design Guidelines — Schematic Checklist (docs.espressif.com, retrieved 2026-10-18)

name: ESP32-C3-WROOM-02 Core (EN reset, BOOT, strapping, native USB)
description: ESP32-C3-WROOM-02 module with EN RC delay, RESET/BOOT buttons, pull-ups on all three strapping pins (GPIO2, GPIO8, GPIO9) per Espressif's checklist, decoupling, and reserved 22 Ω series resistors on native USB (GPIO18 = D−, GPIO19 = D+).

components.notes: Pulls GPIO9 low for download mode
GPIO8 pull-up — must be 1 for download boot
GPIO2 pull-up — Espressif recommends it to avoid boot glitches

design_notes: Boot modes: SPI boot needs GPIO2 = 1 and GPIO9 = 1; download boot needs GPIO2 = 1, GPIO8 = 1, GPIO9 = 0. Anything you attach to GPIO2/8/9 must not override these levels at reset. No large capacitors on GPIO9. GPIO18/GPIO19 are used by native USB.
layout_notes: PCB-antenna keep-out per the module datasheet: antenna at the board edge, no copper beneath it on any layer. Decoupling at pin 1; stitch ground pins with vias.
references: Espressif ESP32-C3 Hardware Design Guidelines — Schematic Checklist (docs.espressif.com, retrieved 2026-10-18)

name: ESP32-C6-MINI-1 Core (Wi-Fi 6, EN reset, BOOT, native USB)
description: ESP32-C6-MINI-1 module with EN RC delay, RESET/BOOT buttons, GPIO9 and GPIO8 strapping pull-ups, decoupling, and reserved 22 Ω series resistors on native USB (GPIO12 = D−, GPIO13 = D+).

components.notes: Pulls GPIO9 low for download mode
GPIO8 pull-up — GPIO8 = 0 with GPIO9 = 0 is an invalid boot state

design_notes: Strapping pins are GPIO8, GPIO9, GPIO15, MTMS and MTDI; check the ESP32-C6 datasheet's Boot Configurations chapter before using GPIO15/MTMS/MTDI at reset. GPIO12/GPIO13 are used by native USB. No large capacitors on GPIO9.
layout_notes: Antenna keep-out per the module datasheet. The many ground pins form the module's thermal/ground pad: tie them to a solid plane with a via array.
references: Espressif ESP32-C6 Hardware Design Guidelines — Schematic Checklist (docs.espressif.com, retrieved 2026-10-18)

name: CH340C USB-UART with ESP32 Auto-Program
description: CH340C USB-to-serial bridge (internal oscillator, no crystal) running at 3.3 V, plus the classic two-transistor DTR/RTS auto-program circuit that drives EN and BOOT so esptool can flash without button presses. For ESP32 parts without native USB (classic ESP32, ESP8266) or to keep native USB free.

components.notes: Built-in oscillator; at 3.3 V supply V3 is tied to VCC

design_notes: CH340 TXD (pin 2) drives the MCU's U0RXD and CH340 RXD (pin 3) receives U0TXD — the net names here already cross them. Each transistor's emitter goes to the other line, so asserting only one of DTR/RTS pulls its target low while asserting both does nothing — this is what lets a terminal program open the port without resetting the board. Keep the MCU core template's EN RC; the transistors simply override it. If the CH340C runs from 5 V instead, put a 100 nF from V3 to GND and do not tie V3 to VCC.
layout_notes: Route USB_DP/USB_DN as a 90 Ω pair from the connector's ESD array. Keep the CH340C close to the USB connector.
references: WCH CH340 datasheet (3.3 V operation, V3 pin)

name: 1-Cell Li-ion Charger (TP4056) with Status LEDs
description: TP4056 linear charger (ESOP-8) for a single 4.2 V Li-ion/LiPo cell from USB 5 V: programmable charge current (2 kΩ → ~580 mA), charging and done LEDs, input and battery capacitors.

components.notes: 4.2 V termination; exposed pad must be soldered to ground copper
Charge current per datasheet table: 10k≈130 mA, 5k≈250 mA, 3k≈400 mA, 2k≈580 mA, 1.5k≈780 mA, 1.2k≈1000 mA. Never exceed 1C of the cell
On when charge is complete (STDBY low)

design_notes: TEMP is tied to GND here, which disables the battery-temperature check; for a product, fit a 10 kΩ NTC divider on TEMP as the datasheet shows. CE is tied to VBUS (always enabled). The TP4056 has no protection against over-discharge or short circuit — add li_ion_protection_dw01a unless the cell has its own protection board. Charging from 5 V to a 3.0 V cell at 1 A dissipates ~2 W; the chip throttles current thermally, so budget copper.
layout_notes: Solder the exposed pad to a large ground pour with thermal vias to the opposite side. Keep R_PROG close to pin 2. Use wide traces for VBUS and BAT+ (calc_trace_width).
references: NanJing Top Power TP4056 datasheet, RPROG table and typical application

name: 1-Cell Li-ion Protection (DW01A + 2× AO3400A)
description: DW01A protection IC with two discrete N-MOSFETs in common-drain configuration: over-charge, over-discharge, over-current and short-circuit protection for a single Li-ion/LiPo cell. The pack negative (PACK−) becomes the system ground.

components.notes: Discharge-control FET (gate from OD); source on cell negative
Charge-control FET (gate from OC); source on PACK−

design_notes: BAT− is the cell's negative terminal only — nothing else connects there. GND here is PACK−: the charger, regulator and the rest of the board return to it. The over-current trip point is set by the FETs' on-resistance (DW01A senses ~150 mV across both), so two AO3400A (~30 mΩ each at 4.5 V gate) trip around 2.5 A; fit lower-RDS(on) FETs for more current. A dual-FET FS8205A is the common integrated alternative.
layout_notes: Keep the BAT−→FET→PACK− path short and wide; it carries the full battery current. Place C_VCC right at pin 5.

name: USB / Battery Load-Sharing Power Path
description: Automatic switchover between USB 5 V and a Li-ion cell: a Schottky feeds the system from USB, and a P-MOSFET connects the battery whenever USB is absent. Lets the board run while the charger charges the cell.

components.notes: P-MOSFET: drain on battery, source on system rail
Schottky from USB to the system rail
Pulls the gate low (FET on) when USB is absent

design_notes: USB present: the gate sits at 5 V, the FET is off and VSYS ≈ VBUS − 0.4 V. USB absent: R_GATE pulls the gate to 0 V and the battery drives VSYS through the FET. The FET's body diode points from battery to VSYS, so the system rail can never back-charge the cell. VSYS ranges ~3.0–4.7 V — feed it to a regulator rated for that input.
layout_notes: Size the Schottky and FET traces for the full system current.
references: Classic load-sharing circuit used on Adafruit/SparkFun Li-ion boards

name: WS2812B Addressable LED with 3.3 V → 5 V Level Shift
description: First WS2812B of a chain at 5 V, driven from a 3.3 V MCU through a 74AHCT1G125 level shifter (TTL input thresholds) and a 330 Ω data resistor, with per-LED and bulk decoupling.

components.notes: 5 V buffer with 2.0 V VIH — accepts 3.3 V logic
Data series resistor, place next to the first LED
First LED; repeat D_LED/C_LED pairs down the chain
One per LED, at its VDD pin
Bulk at the chain's power entry; add 470–1000 µF for long strips

design_notes: WS2812B needs VIH ≥ 0.7·VDD = 3.5 V at 5 V, so a bare 3.3 V GPIO is out of spec — hence the 74AHCT buffer (its ~OE is grounded, so it is always enabled). Each LED draws up to ~60 mA at full white: budget 5 V supply and trace width per LED count (calc_trace_width).
layout_notes: Keep the data line short from the buffer to the first LED; put each 100 nF right at its LED's VDD pin.

name: SHT30 Temperature & Humidity Sensor (I2C)
description: Sensirion SHT30-DIS on I2C at address 0x44 (ADDR to GND), with decoupling and a reset pull-up. Add one pair of bus pull-ups per bus (calc_passive kind 'i2c' or the i2c_pullups template).

components.notes: I2C address 0x44 with ADDR low (0x45 with ADDR high)

design_notes: Pin 7 (R) has no electrical function and is tied to VSS per the datasheet. ALERT is left unconnected; route it to a GPIO if you use the alert mode.
layout_notes: Self-heating ruins humidity readings: keep the sensor away from the regulator, MCU and Wi-Fi module, ideally on a slotted tongue at the board edge with no copper pour around it, and vent the enclosure.
references: Sensirion SHT3x-DIS datasheet, pin assignment and typical application

name: 3.3 V 3 A Buck Converter (TPS563200)
description: TI TPS563200 synchronous buck, 4.5–17 V in, 3.3 V out up to 3 A at 650 kHz, with the datasheet's recommended feedback divider (33.2 kΩ / 10 kΩ), inductor and output capacitance. Replaces an LDO when dissipation is too high (e.g. 5 V/12 V to 3.3 V for an ESP32 with peripherals).

components.notes: Input, X5R/X7R rated ≥25 V (datasheet: >10 µF ceramic) — place at VIN/GND pins
EN pull-up to VIN (EN has ~450 kΩ to GND inside)
Datasheet range for 3.3 V: 1.5–2.2 µH. Saturation current above your peak (calc_buck); match the footprint to the part you buy

design_notes: For 5 V output the datasheet gives R2 = 54.9 kΩ with R3 = 10 kΩ and 2.2–3.3 µH. Input ceramic capacitance shrinks with DC bias: at 12 V use a 25 V or higher part. Check the inductor with calc_buck for your input range and load.
layout_notes: Keep the C_IN → VIN/GND loop as small as possible on the top layer, the SW node short and compact, and route BUCK_FB from the output capacitor away from the inductor and SW. Solid ground under the regulator with vias at C_IN and C_OUT grounds.
references: TI TPS563200 datasheet, Table 8-4 (recommended component values) and Application section, retrieved 2026-10-18

name: Bidirectional I2C Level Shifter (2× BSS138)
description: Classic two-channel bidirectional open-drain level shifter between a low-voltage bus (e.g. 3.3 V ESP32) and a high-voltage bus (e.g. 5 V sensor), one BSS138 N-MOSFET and two pull-ups per line.

components.notes: Gate to LV rail, source on LV side, drain on HV side

design_notes: Works for open-drain buses (I2C, SMBus, 1-Wire) up to about 400 kHz with modest capacitance; 10 kΩ pull-ups are slow — lower them (calc_passive kind 'i2c') for fast mode or long buses. Remove any duplicate pull-ups on sensor modules. Not for push-pull signals such as SPI — use a buffer like 74LVC1T45 there.
layout_notes: Place the MOSFETs near the HV connector so the LV bus stays short.
references: NXP AN10441, Level shifting techniques in I2C-bus design

name: Reverse-Polarity Protection (P-MOSFET ideal diode)
description: Low-loss reverse-polarity protection for a DC input up to about 20 V: AO3401A P-MOSFET in the positive rail with gate pull-down and a 10 V zener gate clamp. Drops millivolts instead of a Schottky's ~0.4 V.

components.notes: 30 V, ~4 A P-MOSFET; drain to input, source to protected rail
Gate pull-down; also limits zener current
Keeps |Vgs| under the AO3401A's 12 V limit; optional when the input never exceeds ~9 V

design_notes: Correct polarity: the body diode conducts first, the gate is pulled 0 V below the source and the FET turns fully on. Reversed: the body diode blocks and the gate is at or above the source, so the FET stays off. Size the MOSFET for the load current and check its dissipation (I² × RDS(on)) with the datasheet's on-resistance at your gate voltage. Add a TVS after the FET for hot-plug transients.
layout_notes: Wide traces for VIN_RAW and VIN (calc_trace_width); the FET carries the full input current.
references: Common P-MOSFET reverse-battery protection topology; Alpha & Omega AO3401A datasheet (VGS ±12 V)
